newsitem.title: USA: Airport Systems sees solid FY97 profit.
newsitem.headline: Airport Systems sees solid FY97 profit.

text.p: Airport Systems International Inc said Monday it expects to report favorable fiscal fourth quarter results versus last year and a solid profit for fiscal 1997.

"Based on our current schedules, we continue to expect a favorable year-to-year comparison in the fourth quarter and believe that results for fiscal 1997 as a whole will include a solid profit for Airport Systems," Keith Cowan, president and chief executive of Airport Systems, said in a statement.
Earlier, Airport Systems which provides products used for aircraft navigation, reported a loss of $0.04 a share for its third quarter ended January 31 versus $0.03 a share last year.
"Though we are clearly unhappy with the loss, over one-half of it, or $53,000 was due to a non-recurring charge of $83,000 during the quarter related to a litigation settlement," Cowan said.
The company said it booked a total of $5.3 million in new business during the fourth quarter.

Airport Systems said it expects to ship much of this equipment before the end of the current fiscal year, but the timing of the receipt of the orders, as well as certain contractual requirements on shipment of the orders, hurt net sales during the third quarter. The impact of the shipmnet deferral on its bottom line was minimized by containing overhead expenses, Airport Systems said.

In addition, the company said progress is being made on an Indonesia contract. Though Airport Systems said there are steps to be completed before financing is finalized, it expects to make shipments on the contract this fiscal year.

"Recent awards of new contracts also have reinforced our strong market position and the opportunities we have to capitalize on the increasing worldwide investment in upgraded air transport navigation systems," Cowan said.
